An approach to unsymmetrical 3,3 ’-
diindolylmethanes through Pd-catalyzed cascade
Heck cyclization of allenamides and
o-ethynylanilines†
Songjin Guo,‡ Jiayi Chen,‡ Mingjun Yi, Liuli Dong, Aijun Lin
 * and Hequan Yao
 *
A highly e ﬃcient synthesis of unsymmetrical 3,3 ’-diindolylmethanes bearing various substituents has
been developed by palladium-catalyzed cascade Heck/cyclization reaction. In this transformation, precur-
sors allenamides and o-ethynylanilines were utilized to generate in situ indole skeletons. Modi ﬁcation of
the methylene unit of diindolylmethane was achieved by treatment with oxidant and silyl nucleophiles.
The methodology allows formation of one C – N bond, two C – C bonds and two new rings in one-pot.
Introduction
Diindolylmethanes (DIMs) are one class of unique and privi-
leged indole alkaloids among numerous natural products,
exhibiting a wide range of biological activities, 1 such as anti-
inflammatory,1a,b antiproliferative,1c antihyperlipidemic,1d
anti-cancer1e and GPR84 agonistic activity. 1f Moreover, DIMs
are also recognized as core building blocks in the research of
colorimetric chemosensors to prepare conjugated tris(indolyl)
methane anion receptors
2 and oxidized-bisindole chromo-
phores3 (Fig. 1).
Owing to their exceptionally potent applications in
materials and pharmaceuticals, the preparation of DIMs has
attracted intensive attention, and several highly e ﬃcient
methods have been developed, in particular those that yield
symmetric DIMs.
4–14 Brønsted or Lewis acids catalysis is the
most straightforward one, wherein key skeleton of DIMs is
forged via the reaction of indoles and alkyl sources, encom-
passing carbonyl compounds, 5 amino acids, 6 alkenes,7
allenes8 and alkynes 9 (Scheme 1a). Besides, photocatalysis, 10
transition metal catalysis, 11 enzyme catalysis, 12 as well as
electrochemical technique 13 have been demonstrated to be
eﬀective strategies for construction of symmetric diindolyl-
methane skeletons (Scheme 1a). In recent years, various
research groups have reported the synthesis of unsymmetrical
DIMs using a leaving group strategy,
14 which is proposed to
proceed through in situ generation of stabilized alkylidenein-
doleninium ion intermediates derived from 3-substituted
indoles (Scheme 1b). Nevertheless, the majority of existing
route employed elaborately pre-functionalized indoles as the
reactants to assemble the symmetrical DIMs system. Thus,
exploring an e ﬀective and practical strategy to rapidly access
diversely unsymmetrical DIMs is still highly desirable, yet chal-
lenging. Based on our continuous interests in the exploration
of indole containing polycyclic synthesis,
15 herein, we will dis-
close an unprecedented palladium-catalyzed cascade Heck/
cyclization reaction between allenamides 16 and o-ethynylani-
lines17 to a ﬀord unsymmetrically substituted 3,3 ′-diindolyl-
methane frameworks. One C –N bond and two C –C bonds
formation can be achieved within one-pot procedure
(Scheme 1c).

Results and discussion
Initial studies were performed with the benchmark substrates
N-allenyl-2-iodoaniline 1a and 4-methyl- N-(2-( phenylethynyl)
phenyl)benzenesulfonamide 2a. Various palladium catalysts
were first tested (Table 1, entries 1 –7). When the reaction was
conducted with Pd(PPh 3)4 as the catalyst in the presence of
Na2CO3 in DMF, the desired product 3aa was isolated in 83%
yield (Table 1, entry 4). The investigation of bases revealed that
K
2CO3 was an ideal choice, which a ﬀorded 3aa in 88% yield
(Table 1, entries 8 –13). The results would be most satisfying
wherein acetonitrile was applied as solvent, while others
(MeOH, DCE, toluene, THF) led to deterioration of the yield
(Table 1, entries 11 and 14 –18). In addition, lowering or
raising the reaction temperature resulted in poor conversion
(Table 1, entries 19 and 20). No expected product could be
detected in the absence of palladium catalyst (Table 1,
entry 21).
The scope of this cascade Heck/cyclization reaction was
next probed, and the results are summarized in Table 2.
Regarding to the N-aryl-N-allenamide 1, we found that
diﬀerent N-protected groups were compatible, the corres-
ponding products ( 3aa–3da) could be isolated in moderate to
good yields. Various substituents, such as methoxyl, methyl,
halogens (F, Cl, Br), and cyano, were well-tolerated to deliver
the products ( 3ea–3na)i n7 0 –98% yields. The methyl-substi-
tuted allene 1o could be converted to 3oa in 78% yield.
Notably, to further increase the molecular diversity, the sub-
strate with pyridine was also investigated, giving 3pa in 92%
yield. A series of o-alkynylanilines bearing substituents with
diﬀerent electronic properties at R
4 participated the reaction
smoothly to deliver the DIMs ( 3ab–3aj)i n5 7 –98% yields. The
structure of the product 3ab was identified by X-ray crystallo-
graphy (see the ESI † for details). It is noteworthy that silyl ( 3al)
and thiophene ( 3am) groups were well tolerated. Products
3an–3as with methyl, methoxyl, trifluoromethyl and halogen
groups ( –F, –Br) groups at the C4- or C5-position of the aryla-
mine were achieved in 50 –91% yields. The o-alkynylaniline 2t
with methyl at the C6-position could not o ﬀer the desired
product 3at. When the substrate 2u with CF 3CO group was
examined, the nitrogen atom deprotected product 3au was
obtained in 50% yield.
In addition to indole sca ﬀolds, other intriguing heteroar-
enes, including isoquinolone 5 and benzofuran 7 were all
formed in 90% and 43% yield respectively by altering the
allene chains (Scheme 2).
Subsequently, to explore the potential utility of this reac-
tion, the scale-up experiments and further transformations of
the diindolylmethane products were conducted as shown in
Table 3. The compounds 3aa (1.14 g) and 3al (0.45 g) could be
prepared in 90% and 72% yield respectively on a millimole
scale (Table 3a). The TMS and sulfamide groups in 3al
could be removed in the present of NaOH, leading to the
symmetric diindolylmethane 8 in 77% yield (Table 3b).
15a
Diindolylmethane 3aa could be smoothly oxidized to 9 with
good e ﬃciency (Table 3c). 18 Compound 10 with a hydroxyl
group was readily achieved in 85% yield through the reduction
of 9 (Table 3d), 19 which served as a versatile intermediate for

plify. Oxidative addition of allenamide 1a to the active Pd(0)
catalyst generates the Pd( II) species I, which undergoes an
intramolecular Heck reaction to achieve the π-allylpalladium
species II.16 The triple bond of o-ethynylaniline 2a coordinates
to intermediate II to produce intermediate III by ligand
exchange. In the presence of base, species III could easily
convert to species IV.17 Finally, the C –C reductive elimination
of species IV produces diindolylmethane 3aa and regenerates
the Pd(0) species to the next catalyzed cycle.
Conclusions
In summary, we have developed a Pd-catalyzed cascade Heck/
cyclization reaction of allenamides and o-ethynylanilines, pro-
viding a straightforward platform to prepare diversified unsym-
metrically substituted 3,3 ′-diindolylmethanes with a modifi-
able methylene in high e ﬃciency. This protocol showcases
good functional group tolerance and scalability. Further trans-
formation of the methylene unit of diindolylmethane was
achieved by treatment with silyl nucleophiles and oxidant. The
reaction proceeded through a sequential alkene insertion, ami-
nopalladation and reductive elimination, involving one C –N
bond, two C –C bonds and two new rings formations.

An approach to unsymmetrical 3,3 ’-
diindolylmethanes through Pd-catalyzed cascade
Heck cyclization of allenamides and
o-ethynylanilines†
Songjin Guo,‡ Jiayi Chen,‡ Mingjun Yi, Liuli Dong, Aijun Lin
 * and Hequan Yao
 *
A highly e ﬃcient synthesis of unsymmetrical 3,3 ’-diindolylmethanes bearing various substituents has
been developed by palladium-catalyzed cascade Heck/cyclization reaction. In this transformation, precur-
sors allenamides and o-ethynylanilines were utilized to generate in situ indole skeletons. Modi ﬁcation of
the methylene unit of diindolylmethane was achieved by treatment with oxidant and silyl nucleophiles.
The methodology allows formation of one C – N bond, two C – C bonds and two new rings in one-pot.
Introduction
Diindolylmethanes (DIMs) are one class of unique and privi-
leged indole alkaloids among numerous natural products,
exhibiting a wide range of biological activities, 1 such as anti-
inflammatory,1a,b antiproliferative,1c antihyperlipidemic,1d
anti-cancer1e and GPR84 agonistic activity. 1f Moreover, DIMs
are also recognized as core building blocks in the research of
colorimetric chemosensors to prepare conjugated tris(indolyl)
methane anion receptors
2 and oxidized-bisindole chromo-
phores3 (Fig. 1).
Owing to their exceptionally potent applications in
materials and pharmaceuticals, the preparation of DIMs has
attracted intensive attention, and several highly e ﬃcient
methods have been developed, in particular those that yield
symmetric DIMs.
4–14 Brønsted or Lewis acids catalysis is the
most straightforward one, wherein key skeleton of DIMs is
forged via the reaction of indoles and alkyl sources, encom-
passing carbonyl compounds, 5 amino acids, 6 alkenes,7
allenes8 and alkynes 9 (Scheme 1a). Besides, photocatalysis, 10
transition metal catalysis, 11 enzyme catalysis, 12 as well as
electrochemical technique 13 have been demonstrated to be
eﬀective strategies for construction of symmetric diindolyl-
methane skeletons (Scheme 1a). In recent years, various
research groups have reported the synthesis of unsymmetrical
DIMs using a leaving group strategy,
14 which is proposed to
proceed through in situ generation of stabilized alkylidenein-
doleninium ion intermediates derived from 3-substituted
indoles (Scheme 1b). Nevertheless, the majority of existing
route employed elaborately pre-functionalized indoles as the
reactants to assemble the symmetrical DIMs system. Thus,
exploring an e ﬀective and practical strategy to rapidly access
diversely unsymmetrical DIMs is still highly desirable, yet chal-
lenging. Based on our continuous interests in the exploration
of indole containing polycyclic synthesis,
15 herein, we will dis-
close an unprecedented palladium-catalyzed cascade Heck/
cyclization reaction between allenamides 16 and o-ethynylani-
lines17 to a ﬀord unsymmetrically substituted 3,3 ′-diindolyl-
methane frameworks. One C –N bond and two C –C bonds
formation can be achieved within one-pot procedure
(Scheme 1c).

Results and discussion
Initial studies were performed with the benchmark substrates
N-allenyl-2-iodoaniline 1a and 4-methyl- N-(2-( phenylethynyl)
phenyl)benzenesulfonamide 2a. Various palladium catalysts
were first tested (Table 1, entries 1 –7). When the reaction was
conducted with Pd(PPh 3)4 as the catalyst in the presence of
Na2CO3 in DMF, the desired product 3aa was isolated in 83%
yield (Table 1, entry 4). The investigation of bases revealed that
K
2CO3 was an ideal choice, which a ﬀorded 3aa in 88% yield
(Table 1, entries 8 –13). The results would be most satisfying
wherein acetonitrile was applied as solvent, while others
(MeOH, DCE, toluene, THF) led to deterioration of the yield
(Table 1, entries 11 and 14 –18). In addition, lowering or
raising the reaction temperature resulted in poor conversion
(Table 1, entries 19 and 20). No expected product could be
detected in the absence of palladium catalyst (Table 1,
entry 21).
The scope of this cascade Heck/cyclization reaction was
next probed, and the results are summarized in Table 2.
Regarding to the N-aryl-N-allenamide 1, we found that
diﬀerent N-protected groups were compatible, the corres-
ponding products ( 3aa–3da) could be isolated in moderate to
good yields. Various substituents, such as methoxyl, methyl,
halogens (F, Cl, Br), and cyano, were well-tolerated to deliver
the products ( 3ea–3na)i n7 0 –98% yields. The methyl-substi-
tuted allene 1o could be converted to 3oa in 78% yield.
Notably, to further increase the molecular diversity, the sub-
strate with pyridine was also investigated, giving 3pa in 92%
yield. A series of o-alkynylanilines bearing substituents with
diﬀerent electronic properties at R
4 participated the reaction
smoothly to deliver the DIMs ( 3ab–3aj)i n5 7 –98% yields. The
structure of the product 3ab was identified by X-ray crystallo-
graphy (see the ESI † for details). It is noteworthy that silyl ( 3al)
and thiophene ( 3am) groups were well tolerated. Products
3an–3as with methyl, methoxyl, trifluoromethyl and halogen
groups ( –F, –Br) groups at the C4- or C5-position of the aryla-
mine were achieved in 50 –91% yields. The o-alkynylaniline 2t
with methyl at the C6-position could not o ﬀer the desired
product 3at. When the substrate 2u with CF 3CO group was
examined, the nitrogen atom deprotected product 3au was
obtained in 50% yield.
In addition to indole sca ﬀolds, other intriguing heteroar-
enes, including isoquinolone 5 and benzofuran 7 were all
formed in 90% and 43% yield respectively by altering the
allene chains (Scheme 2).
Subsequently, to explore the potential utility of this reac-
tion, the scale-up experiments and further transformations of
the diindolylmethane products were conducted as shown in
Table 3. The compounds 3aa (1.14 g) and 3al (0.45 g) could be
prepared in 90% and 72% yield respectively on a millimole
scale (Table 3a). The TMS and sulfamide groups in 3al
could be removed in the present of NaOH, leading to the
symmetric diindolylmethane 8 in 77% yield (Table 3b).
15a
Diindolylmethane 3aa could be smoothly oxidized to 9 with
good e ﬃciency (Table 3c). 18 Compound 10 with a hydroxyl
group was readily achieved in 85% yield through the reduction
of 9 (Table 3d), 19 which served as a versatile intermediate for

catalyst generates the Pd( II) species I, which undergoes an
intramolecular Heck reaction to achieve the π-allylpalladium
species II.16 The triple bond of o-ethynylaniline 2a coordinates
to intermediate II to produce intermediate III by ligand
exchange. In the presence of base, species III could easily

of species IV produces diindolylmethane 3aa and regenerates
the Pd(0) species to the next catalyzed cycle.
Conclusions
In summary, we have developed a Pd-catalyzed cascade Heck/
cyclization reaction of allenamides and o-ethynylanilines, pro-
viding a straightforward platform to prepare diversified unsym-
metrically substituted 3,3 ′-diindolylmethanes with a modifi-
able methylene in high e ﬃciency. This protocol showcases
good functional group tolerance and scalability. Further trans-
formation of the methylene unit of diindolylmethane was
achieved by treatment with silyl nucleophiles and oxidant. The
reaction proceeded through a sequential alkene insertion, ami-
nopalladation and reductive elimination, involving one C –N
bond, two C –C bonds and two new rings formations.
